narrative.intro: Softrams has $217M in contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Softrams has 18 awards and an average award size of $12M. Softrams obligations are up 4.8% year over year. Softrams obligations increased from $70.2M in FY21 to $217M in FY26, with interim totals of $77.7M in FY22, $125M in FY23, $158M in FY24, and $207M in FY25. The Department of Health and Human Services is the largest buying agency for Softrams in FY2026 to date with $177M obligated. The Department of Veterans Affairs has obligated $25.9M, and the Department of Homeland Security has obligated $13.4M. Softrams sells work in Custom Computer Programming Services and Computer Systems Design Services, which have obligations of $182M and $34.8M respectively. The current-year totals are partial (fiscal year to date).

sections.heading: Who are Softrams's top buying agencies?
sections.body: The Department of Health and Human Services has obligated $177M to Softrams in FY2026 to date. The Department of Veterans Affairs has obligated $25.9M to Softrams and the Department of Homeland Security has obligated $13.4M to Softrams. The General Services Administration has obligated $279K to Softrams.

sections.heading: How has Softrams's federal business trended over recent fiscal years?
sections.body: Softrams obligations rose from $70.2M in FY21 to $217M in FY26. Softrams had $77.7M in FY22, $125M in FY23, $158M in FY24, and $207M in FY25. Softrams obligations are up 4.8% year over year.

faq.q: How much does Softrams make from federal contracts?
faq.a: Softrams has $217M in federal contract obligations in FY2026 to date. Softrams has 18 awards and an average award size of $12M, and Softrams obligations are up 4.8% year over year.

The Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and the Department of Homeland Security are the top buyers of Softrams in FY2026 to date. The Department of Health and Human Services has obligated $177M, the Department of Veterans Affairs has obligated $25.9M, and the Department of Homeland Security has obligated $13.4M. The General Services Administration has obligated $279K.

faq.q: What does Softrams sell to the government?
faq.a: Softrams sells Custom Computer Programming Services and Computer Systems Design Services to the government. Custom Computer Programming Services has $182M in obligations and Computer Systems Design Services has $34.8M in obligations.
